newsitem.title: USA: House file probers say FBI counsel should quit.
newsitem.headline: House file probers say FBI counsel should quit.

text.p: A House panel late Tuesday adopted an interim report on the White House's mishandling of FBI files and called for a top FBI official to resign.
The report was approved by the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee over the protests of Democrats, who charged it was politically motivated.

The committee has been investigating the improper acquisition by the White House office of personnel security of hundreds of FBI files on Republicans in 1993 and 1994. The investigation, begun last May, was an outgrowth of its inquiry into the 1993 firing of the White House travel office.

In its report on the so-called "filegate affair," the panel accused FBI General Counsel Howard Shapiro of improper contacts with the White House in alerting it to allegations that Hillary Rodham Clinton was involved in recommending the hiring of the former head of the personnel office, Craig Livingstone.

"Even though a complete review of Shapiro's activities has not been completed, it is clear from the evidence available to the committee that Shapiro's actions were grossly inappropriate and he should, therefore, resign," the report summary said.
It noted that Shapiro -- in whom FBI Director Louis Freeh has expressed confidence -- had acknowledged that his "heads up" to the White House was inappropriate.
"However, his cosiness with the White House continues," the report said. "Even the perception of such a relationship threatens the independence of the FBI."

The report said the White House review of files of political appointees of the Ronald Reagan and George Bush administrations "leads to the possibility that the Clinton administration was attempting to prepare a political 'hit list' or 'enemies list.'"
The White House has said that the acquisition of the files was the result of innocent confusion.
"The committee has yet to determine whether colossal incompetence or sinister motive precipitated these events," the report said.
Committee Chairman William Clinger, a Pennsylvania Republican, said the question of who hired Livingstone was still to be answered.
The committee's top Democrat, Cardiss Collins of Illinois, termed the release of the report now "one more committee contribution to the (Republican presidential candidate Bob) Dole campaign."
